text:
elena: Heads up — we need a concrete plan for KMS key rotation across AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault. Seen two edge-cases in staging: old ciphertext becomes unreadable after a naive rewrap when the envelope header version increments, and some long-lived clients with pinned KV cache keep referencing the old KEK. Need recommendations for automatic vs manual rewrap windows, RBAC changes, audit log hooks, and rollback playbook. @samir @alia any immediate thoughts?

samir: Agree. Two main thrusts: dual-read compatibility + staged rewrap. I suggest we keep envelope header versioning and support a "read-legacy" path for N months. Automatic rotation of customer KEKs can be frequent (90d), but rewrap of stored ciphertext should be staged and observable.

alia: RBAC notes: create a scoped permission like kms:reencrypt and kms:rewrap on Redwood service accounts. Don't blanket give kms:encrypt/decrypt to app roles. For AWS map to a cross-account role with sts:AssumeRole, for GCP use a service account with roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on the target key, and on Azure grant Key Vault access policy for wrapKey/unwrapKey to the platform principal. Also require an "approval" label for any non-canary bulk rewraps.

marco: Rollout phases I've used successfully:
1) Canary: rewrap a tiny subset (0.5% of keys or a few user buckets) for 24-48h.
2) Linear ramp: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% over a week with health gates.
3) Post-100%: keep legacy-read enabled for a 30-90 day grace window, then retire legacy readers.
Health gates: decryption_error_rate, 5xx rate, latency 95p. If any gate trips, immediate pause + rollback.

elena: What does rollback look like? Rewrap is destructive sometimes. We need an explicit safe-path.

samir: Two rollback options depending on whether we kept the original ciphertext footprint:
- Preferred (non-destructive): For every rewrap we store original_ciphertext reference and the wrapping_key_version in metadata. Rolling back means re-wrapping the new ciphertext back to the old KEK using stored original metadata OR unwrapping to plaintext via KMS audit (if allowed) then re-encrypting with old KEK. This requires we have retained access to old KEK (do NOT deprecate until grace window ends).
- Emergency: If we didn't store originals, we must restore from backups (S3/GCS snapshots) and abort. So backups are mandatory for bulk rewrap.

# example canary command (pseudo)
```bash
# dry-run first
redwood-kms rewrap --source-key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123:key/abc --target-key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123:key/def --filter prefix=canary/ --dry-run
# execute canary
redwood-kms rewrap --source-key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123:key/abc --target-key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123:key/def --filter prefix=canary/ --concurrency 4
```

alia: Observability / audit: ensure each rewrap emits structured audit events (can push to CloudTrail / Cloud Audit Logs / Azure Monitor) and we forward to our central audit sink. Event shape suggestion: {"event_type":"key_rewrap","actor":"<principal>","key_id":"<key>","phase":"canary|ramp|complete","status":"started|success|failed","affected_objects":n}. Make sure logs include key version identifiers and request IDs for correlation.

marco: Also mind envelope header versioning. Implement schema that includes: version, kek_id, algorithm, original_version_tag. When reading, attempt read-new, then read-legacy. Avoid schema breaking changes without explicit migration.

ops-bot: Deploy-note: rewrap-run initiated by elena at 2025-07-14T17:03:12Z (dry-run).

elena: Good. Next actions: can someone draft a concise runbook with concrete RBAC changes + audit example + canary commands? I want a short RFC for compliance with timings (canary window, ramp cadence, grace window).

samir: I'll draft the runbook and include a short checklist: verify backups, create a temporary rewrap role with least privilege, kick off dry-run, monitor defined metrics for 48h, then proceed to canary.

alia: I'll add IAM policy snippets for AWS/GCP/Azure and the approval workflow (ticket + manager + 2FA).

marco: I'll produce the health-gate alert queries and recommended thresholds (decryption_error_rate > 0.01% -> pause, 5xx increase > 2x baseline -> pause).

elena: Awesome — please post runbook RFC in #eng-security and tag me.

samir: ack, aiming EOD tomorrow.
